transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-01
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: 52m
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Alex (CTO, KilnWorks), Priya (Head Infra), Sam (Security Lead)
Recording link: https://redwood.fireflies/fake-link/KW-20260901

Summary:
KilnWorks is evaluating Redwood for LLM inference across Hosted/Dedicated/Private; primary blockers are SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML provisioning, RBAC granularity, audit log retention/export, and KMS/bring-your-own-key flow. They prefer Dedicated for pilot but need clarity on on-prem/private path for PHI-like data.

Topics: SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML/SCIM, RBAC, audit logs (real-time or export), encryption/KMS (BYOK/HSM), data residency & retention, rollout timeline and benchmarks.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hi everyone, thanks for carving out time. I'm Jordan, AE on the infra team, and with me is Maya, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Alex (KilnWorks CTO): Good, thanks. Quick context: we're building an assistant for our manuf line support, could hit a few thousand requests per minute at peak, and our compliance team cares a lot about keys, retention, and SOC/ISO.
[00:28] Maya (Redwood SE): Great, that's helpful. High level — we support three deployment modes: Hosted API, Dedicated reserved GPU pools, and Private (VPC or on-prem). Each has different tradeoffs on isolation and operational responsibility.
[00:40] Priya (Head Infra): Can you quickly outline the security docs you have? SOC2, ISO? We need to feed that to our risk committee.
[00:50] Jordan: Yep — we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001. I'll share a summary pack and the attestation reports. Our hosted plane is SOC2 covered; Dedicated contracts can be included in enterprise terms.
[01:05] Sam (Security): A couple of specifics we care about: do you support customer-managed keys (BYOK) and HSM-backed key storage? And what about key rotation/rotation proofs?
[01:18] Maya: For Hosted we support CMEK via major cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) with BYOK patterns — keys in customer account via cross-account grants, and we also offer a Private option where keys never leave your environment. HSM-backed KMS is supported if your provider/KMS offers it. Rotation — we support key rotation workflows and can provide logs that show key usage; for Private you control rotation.
[01:45] Alex: For the pilot, we were leaning Dedicated — predictable latency and cost. With Dedicated, who controls keys? Are we forced to hand keys to Redwood?
[01:55] Maya: Dedicated can be set up with customer keys depending on deployment. In cloud Dedicated, we can integrate with your KMS; for on-prem Private, you keep keys. We never require keys for data-in-transit encryption, obviously.
[02:10] Priya: Audit logs: can we stream logs to Splunk or S3? What's retention by default?
[02:18] Jordan: Default audit retention for hosted is 90 days for detailed token-level traces; aggregated metrics available longer. We can provide exports to your SIEM (SPLUNK) via webhook or S3 export for longer retention. Dedicated/Private give you more control over retention policies.
[02:35] Sam: Okay, but we need immutable audit records for 1 year for some PII flows. Is that possible? Also, are logs pseudonymized?
[02:43] Maya: Yes — we have export pipelines. For PII you can configure redaction and tokenization at the ingestion path. For immutability we recommend export to your S3 with object locking or to your SIEM. We can maintain append-only logs on our side for a shorter window but the canonical record for long-term retention should be in your storage.
[03:05] Alex: What about RBAC? We have devs, ops, and a security group that needs read-only audit access. How granular is it?
[03:13] Maya: RBAC is role-based with predefined roles (admin, operator, developer, auditor). We also support custom roles at the org and team level in the Console. You can scope per-route and per-model. For larger customers we map to SAML groups via SCIM provisioning so mapping is automated.
[03:30] Priya: SAML/SSO — we use Okta. How does SSO onboarding work? Can we do IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows? SCIM for user provisioning?
[03:40] Jordan: Yes, we support SAML 2.0 with both flows and SCIM for user and group provisioning. We also support enforced MFA and can integrate with your enterprise policy. We will provide SAML metadata and a test IdP setup in the sandbox.
[03:58] Sam: On the security questionnaire front — we have a fairly long vendor risk survey. Do you have a completed standard vendor pack we can use?
[04:07] Jordan: We have a security questionnaire pack and a standard ISO/SOC attestation bundle. I'll attach that after the call. For anything not covered, Maya can run through the answers with you or we can do a deep-dive.
[04:20] Alex: Can we talk about data residency? Some of our data must stay in EU.
[04:26] Maya: We have region controls — hosted model can be pinned to regions and we have infra in EU regions. For strict residency we recommend Dedicated in your chosen region or Private VPC/on-prem.
[04:40] Priya: For Dedicated latency — what's the SLA and how do you handle failover across regions?
[04:47] Maya: Dedicated offers a latency and uptime SLA in the enterprise contract. Failover strategies include cross-region standby and automatic fallback to compatible model variants in another region, but that will impact latency and may have data residency implications.
[05:05] Alex: If we go Private (on-prem), what's the control plane like? Is it a customer-managed control plane or do we still talk to Redwood for upgrades?
[05:14] Maya: For Private, the control plane can be customer-hosted or a hybrid with a minimal control channel. Patches and upgrades can be automated through your ops channels or handled by Redwood under a managed agreement. For air-gapped setups we provide installable bundles and upgrade scripts.
[05:36] Sam: For encryption in transit and at rest, what ciphers and protocols do you use? And are TLS certs customer-managed?
[05:45] Jordan: We use industry standard TLS 1.2/1.3 for transit. At rest we rely on KMS and cloud provider encryption. For Dedicated/Private you can bring certs; for hosted we manage certs with Let's Encrypt or provider-managed certs, but we can also support customer-provided certs for enterprise customers.
[06:05] Priya: Pen tests/compliance: do you do third-party penetration tests and can we get the results or a summary?
[06:12] Maya: We perform annual third-party pentests and can share summarized findings and attestations. Full reports are typically available under NDA.
[06:25] Alex: A bit naive question — when you say token-level logs, is that actual model input and full responses? We have to avoid storing full PII outputs.
[06:34] Maya: By default, token traces may include full request/response for debugging in a short retention window. We can configure to strip or hash inputs, or not capture them at all. For PHI/PII workloads we recommend disabling full transcript logging and using hashed identifiers and request sampling. We'll note that in the pilot playbook.
[06:55] Sam: How easy is it to do data deletion requests (e.g., subject access or right to be forgotten)?
[07:02] Jordan: We have procedures to support data deletion — on hosted we can delete request traces and associated ephemeral cache within defined windows, and can provide certificates of deletion for exported logs. For Dedicated/Private you control deletion if logs are in your account.
[07:17] Alex: On the model side, can we pin versions for rollouts and do canary traffic splits?
[07:24] Maya: Yes — our rollout features support version pinning, canary, A/B, and automatic rollback. You can set traffic percentages and schedule rollouts in the Console or via API.
[07:36] Priya: Pricing & cost units — if we do a Dedicated pool, how granular are the metrics? We need per-team cost allocation.
[07:44] Jordan: The Console provides token-level and route-level cost attribution, invoices by org and optional per-route tags. Dedicated can be metered by reservation buckets and per-route usage.
[07:56] Alex: Ok. Could we setup a short benchmark with a synthetic workload next week? We want to measure p50/p95 latency and sustained throughput.
[08:03] Maya: Absolutely — Maya: we can provision a small Dedicated queue for that, run a 2-hour loadgen, and share the results. We'll need sample prompts and target concurrency.
[08:15] Sam: For the benchmark, can we also capture end-to-end tracing so we can match logs between our app and the inference path?
[08:22] Maya: Yes — we can pass trace IDs and provide request IDs in our logs to correlate. We also support OpenTelemetry hooks.
[08:33] Alex: Any restrictions around model weights or data residency for custom models? We plan to fine-tune a model with internal support transcripts.
[08:42] Maya: For Hosted we manage model artifacts; fine-tuning workflows are handled in isolated spaces with controls. For Dedicated/Private you can bring your fine-tuned models; on Private the artifacts never leave your environment unless you opt-in.
[08:58] Jordan: Quick note: competitors? anything you're comparing us to that we should be aware of?
[09:03] Alex: We looked at Anthropic's infra, AWS Bedrock, and a self-hosted Triton approach. Biggest differences are operational overhead for self-host and the guardrails/certificates you provide.
[09:18] Maya: Good to know. We'll highlight the operational tradeoffs in the follow-up doc.
[09:25] Priya: A question about RBAC audit: can we get a stream of admin events only to our security team? e.g., role changes, keys creation, SSO provisioning, service principal changes etc.
[09:36] Maya: Yes — event filters can be configured. We can send admin events to a distinct webhook or to your SIEM. We also produce change logs in the Console with who/when/what.
[09:50] Sam: Are there encryption attestations for at-rest encryption other than the provider cert? Like FIPS-140-2 HSM attestation?
[09:58] Jordan: For HSM-backed keys we can provide attestations from the KMS provider. We don't operate our own HSM for hosted keys; for Private you can run your own HSM and supply attestation.
[10:12] Alex: Onboarding time — if we want a 4-week pilot with Dedicated, what's the path?
[10:18] Jordan: Typical steps: sign an MSA + DPA, sandbox access and SSO + SCIM setup, Dedicated pool provisioning (1-3 days), pilot benchmark + eval (1 week), security review and SOC artifacts (parallel), then go/no-go at end of pilot. We'll prepare a project plan.
[10:34] Priya: DPA — does Redwood support our standard DPA and any custom clauses about subprocessing?
[10:41] Jordan: We have a standard DPA; we're used to negotiating subprocessor clauses for enterprise customers — we will review your template.
[10:50] Maya: Also to add — regarding KV cache and prefix caching: if you want to avoid caching of specific prompts, we can disable certain cache behaviors or set TTLs. Important for PII.
[10:58] Alex: Good. A few technical nitty-gritty items for the SE deep-dive: how do you manage kv cache isolation across tenants on multi-tenant hosted?
[11:06] Maya: We isolate KV caches per-tenant and shard them; for cryptographic isolation we rely on per-tenant encryption keys for cached artifacts. For Dedicated there's full process isolation at the workload level.
[11:20] Sam: What about tracing latency overhead if we enable full-token logs? Might add 10-20%?
[11:26] Maya: There is some overhead. In our runs enabling detailed tracing added measurable overhead; we usually surface token traces on sampling to limit impact. For critical audits we recommend exporting a sampled subset to your SIEM.
[11:42] Alex: Ok let's outline next steps — we want: SOC2/ISO artifacts, an estimate for Dedicated pilot pricing, benchmark run next week, and SSO test setup.
[11:52] Jordan: I'll send the SOC/ISO bundle and contract starter. Maya will prepare the benchmark playbook and a proposed config. Also we'll schedule the SAML test — can you provision an Okta test org?
[12:05] Priya: Yes we'll spin up a test Okta tenant and share SAML metadata. We'll also send the retention matrix and which data classes require 1-year retention.
[12:15] Sam: For action items on our side: we'll identify stakeholders for the pilot and circle back on legal review timeline.
[12:24] Jordan: Great. Anything else before we wrap?
[12:28] Alex: One final: are you able to provide a short architecture diagram of Dedicated vs Private flows to show to our legal folks?
[12:35] Maya: Yes — I'll include a diagram in the follow-up packet showing network flows, where keys live, and logging/export paths.
[12:44] Jordan: Perfect. Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the packets and a proposed calendar invite for the benchmark.
[12:50] Alex: Thanks — talk soon.

Call end.
